hooks.text: Our galaxy is falling toward an invisible cosmic monster.
What invisible cosmic giant is pulling the Milky Way through space?
We are falling toward an invisible mass at 1.3 million miles per hour.

title: The Unseen Force Dragging the Milky Way
description: The Milky Way is hurtling toward a massive unseen region of space. But the force pulling us is even larger than we ever imagined.

beats.text: Our galaxy is falling toward an invisible cosmic monster.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of the Milky Way being pulled by gravity

beats.text: We are hurtling through the dark at 1.3 million miles per hour.
beats.visual: map of galaxy peculiar velocity flow vectors in the local universe

beats.text: For decades, the thick gas and dust of the Milky Way completely blocked our view of this giant.
beats.visual: panoramic telescope image of the dusty plane of the Milky Way

beats.text: In the 1980s, astronomers used infrared and X-ray telescopes to finally pierce this barrier.
beats.visual: photograph of the Parkes Observatory radio telescope in Australia

beats.text: They discovered the Great Attractor, a gravitational basin holding around 100,000 galaxies.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of the Norma Cluster Abell 3627

beats.text: But astronomers quickly realized this region has far too little mass to cause such a violent pull.
beats.visual: scientific map of the Laniakea Supercluster flow lines

beats.text: Instead, a much larger titan called the Shapley Supercluster is dragging the entire region.
beats.visual: deep space image of the massive Shapley Supercluster

beats.text: Cosmic expansion will eventually pull us away, but for now, we continue our plunge.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the expanding universe driven by dark energy

better_than_last: Used a clean record structure starting directly with the speed record of our cosmic fall to maximize viewer retention.
